name: Should I frame an interior partition wall with wood or metal studs?

mainEntity.name: Should I frame an interior partition wall with wood or metal studs?

acceptedAnswer.text: Wood studs (traditionally 2x4 framing) offer superior structural rigidity for hanging heavy items like floating vanities, upper cabinetry, grab bars, or wall-mounted televisions without special toggle hardware. Steel studs are lightweight, fire-resistant, and stay straight without warping or bowing, making them useful in commercial builds or damp basements. The tradeoff is that light-gauge metal studs require backing reinforcement or plywood plates installed inside the framing cavities before drywall if you plan to mount solid shelving, heavy mirrors, or interior doors securely.
acceptedAnswer.description: Wood provides better anchor strength for heavy shelves and cabinets, while steel framing resists warping and rot but requires pre-installed backing plates for secure mounting.
